THM 105.name: Service Business Management
THM 105.description: Developing a Business Mindset, Business Ethics and Corporate Responsibility, Forms of Ownership, Entrepreneurship and Small-Business Ownership, Management Roles, Functions and Skills, Organization and Teamwork, Service Encounter and the Service Quality, Employee Motivation, Human Resources Management, The Art and Science of Marketing for Service Businesses, Product and Pricing Strategies, Customer Communication.

THM 106.name: Principles of Accounting
THM 106.description: The course introduces the business environment, basic mechanics of record keeping and reporting of financial statement information. The topics covered include the generally accepted accounting principles, the accounting cycle, preparation and reporting of financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, and statement of shareholders' equity). The course aims to familiarize students with various tools and techniques that are currently used in accounting. Widely used accounting software tools will be used for recording transactions and preparation of financial statements.

THM 121.name: Business Mathematics
THM 121.description: This course aims to teach students the basics of Algebra. In this regard, students will be acquainted with Operations with fractions and ratio / proportions as well as operations with algebraic expressions. Moreover, students will gain necessary skills helping them to factorize polynomials, solve linear equations and absolute value inequalities. Lastly, students will learn about functions (lines and linear functions, limits, graphs and continuity).

THM 125.name: Introduction to Tourism and Hospitality in the Digital Age
THM 125.description: UNWTO Tourism Highlights: Understanding the economic impact of the tourism industry; fundamentals of tourism terminology, the Destination, characteristics of successful destinations, attractions as main attributes of destinations, Sustainable destinations and policies; basic concepts and terminology of sustainable development, Intermediaries, distribution channels, virtual distributors and the digital tools, Transportation, air, ground and sea transportation, importance of each mode in tourism industry, airports, Tourism demand, Overview of the hospitality industry, Human Resources and IT technologies, Accounting and IT technologies, Sales and Marketing and agreements with OTA's, use of social media, The Front Office and IT technologies / Fidelio / Opera, Housekeeping, Food and Beverage and IT technologies / Fidelio / MC, Property Operation and Maintenance, Personal Safety and Property Security, contemporary surveillance systems.

THM 163.name: Dynamics of Tourism
THM 163.description: The position of tourism as the world's largest industry which has led to the widespread acknowledgment of the decisive role it plays in shaping the world. A global overview of the industry; trends, its socio-cultural and economic impact, motivators, hospitality related services, transportation, intermediaries and attractions.

THM 164.name: Calculus
THM 164.description: Provides background knowledge of mathematical procedures that are designed to analyze numerical information essential in decision making, for those who intend to pursue a career in hospitality management. Topics include: linear and quadratic equations; rate of change of functions; derivatives and integration.

THM 166.name: Health Studies
THM 166.description: The knowledge and skills necessary to help people whose first-aid problems have to be addressed promptly and properly. Conducted by the professionals of the Ministry of Health in its facilities and a required passing grade for completion.

THM 168.name: Nutrition and Sanitation
THM 168.description: Introduction to sanitation, Foodborne illnesses, Contamination- Spoilage - Thawing - Preservation methods, Purchasing and Storage, Personal hygiene of foodhandler, Pest - control and H.A.C.C.P, Training, Introduction to nutrition, Metabolism and energy balance, Carbohydrates - alcohol - artificial sweeteners, Proteins and Vegetarianism, Lipids : Triglycerides - Phospholipids /Sterols, Vitamins and Minerals : Water soluble vitamins - Fat soluble vitamins - Major minerals- trace minerals.

THM 172.name: World Travel Destinations
THM 172.description: Familiarization of students with popular tourist destinations and their attractions in order to understand and determine the needs, interests and expectations of tourists. Major land forms, time zones, international travel flows, and world's top tourism destinations as well as related major attractions.

THM 202.name: Principles of Management
THM 202.description: Insights into the basic managerial functions, primarily planning, organizing, leading and controlling. History of management with the basic premise to relate the past to the present and encourage the students to investigate and learn unified, universal, valid principles and theories applicable in the field.

THM 242.name: Social Psychology
THM 242.description: Includes some of the fundamental components of the study of tourism from a social-psychological standpoint. The course will study tourism along two dimensions: by an understanding of the social, organizational and the community contexts of tourism.

THM 243.name: Rooms Division Management
THM 243.description: Hotel Organization, Front Office Operations, Reservations, Registration, Front Office Accounting, Check-out and Account Settlement, The Role of Housekeeping in Hospitality Operations, Pricing, Forecasting, Rooms Division Department Operational Issues, Budgeting.

THM 244.name: Food Production Techniques
THM 244.description: Most common tools and equipment and basic methods used in the preparation of foods. Various products used with common basic preparation methods; use and interpretation of recipes, as well as planning menus considering the traditional organization of medium to large kitchen operations.

THM 245.name: Purchasing and Cost Analysis
THM 245.description: Skills and knowledge for effective management of purchasing and cost analysis in a hotel. Determination of standards, development of operating budget, cost-volume-profit analysis, as well as basic operating activities, such as menu planning, purchasing, receiving, storing, issuing, production and serving. Knowledge required to prepare food and beverage reconciliation reports.

THM 246.name: Restaurant Service
THM 246.description: Knowledge for effective management of food and beverage services. Conducted in two sessions. First, theoretical knowledge before the service starts, then experience by working in a fine dining room. (Le Piment Rouge Restaurant.)

THM 247.name: Food and Beverage Management
THM 247.description: Basic service principles and knowledge for budgeting and effective management of food service operations. Restaurant marketing, menu analysis, menu pricing strategies and guest relations.

THM 252.name: Tourist Attractions of Turkey
THM 252.description: Regional distribution of touristic activities with an emphasis on the natural, historical and archaeological attractions along with their characteristics as tourism products in Turkey. The field trip to selected destinations being an integral part the course.

THM 300.name: Summer Internship
THM 300.description: An intensive exposure to the tourism workplace and hands-on-experience in tourism related fields.
THM 300.prerequisite: THM 125 and THM 243 and THM 245 and THM 247

THM 301.name: Human Resources Management
THM 301.description: Basic knowledge in human resources field. Equal employee opportunities and law, job analysis and job design, personal planning and recruiting, employee testing and selection, interviewing candidates, training and developing employees, evaluating employee performance, and pay for performance and financial incentives.

THM 302.name: Human Resources Analytics and Applications
THM 302.description: Equal Employment Opportunities and Laws. Legal issues and ethics. Inclusions. Diversity. Data driven decision making and HR analytics. Job Analysis. Occupational Information Network (O'NET). Job Description/Job Specification. Metrics and measures for workforce planning. Recruitment. Placement. Talent management. Employee selection tests. Validity and reliability. Interview process. Performance management and appraisal. Training and development. Managing employee retention. Establishing strategic pay plans. Linking performance rating to compensation. Labor relations and collective bargaining. Big Data. HR metrics. HR measures. HR Analytics. HR functions applications.

THM 303.name: Statistics and Quantitative Methods
THM 303.description: Statistics and its role in managerial decision making, discrete and continuous numerical data, level of measurement for numerical data, graphical description of data, descriptive measures, basic counting rules, probability concepts, discrete probability distributions, continuous probability distributions; standard, normal, t, chi square and f distribution, sampling and statistical inference, hypothesis testing, bivariate data, regression, correlation.

THM 309.name: Principles of Marketing
THM 309.description: Basic marketing concepts and principles considering the major trends and forces impacting marketing in today's high-tech era of customer value and relationships. Strategic marketing planning, segmentation, target marketing and positioning, understanding consumer behavior, new product development and product life cycle strategies and developing the marketing mix. A practical marketing-management approach and a number of real-life examples and stories that show how those basic concepts and principles are put into action in today's modern marketing world with the help of the case studies covered.

THM 310.name: Semester Internship
THM 310.description: One semester work in the industry. An opportunity to apply acquired theoretical knowledge to a real-life environment as well as to observe, document and evaluate the operations in tourism and hotel related entities.

THM 313.name: Hospitality Management Accounting
THM 313.description: Main issues in management accounting. Hotel revenue accounting: revenue accounts, operational and non-operational revenues, Internal control of revenues, Hotel revenue accounting (industry practice), VAT applications, journal entry of front office transactions, journal entry of rebates, journal entry of food and beverage sales, daily general cashier report, journal entry of cash transactions, hotel expense accounting, financial information system, classification of expenses and payroll-related expenses, hotel departmental statements / schedules, hotel income statement, Property and equipment accounting, other non-current assets accounting, hotel balance sheet, statement of cash flows, operational budget, ratio analysis, and inventory accounting.

THM 323.name: International Cuisines
THM 323.description: Work (as small groups) in a luxurious restaurant's kitchen. The opportunity to prepare different menus from a variety of well-known international cuisines.

THM 324.name: World's Culinary Cultures
THM 324.description: Evolution of man and periods. Nutrition habits of countries and differences. World religions and their effects on nutrition habits. Eating habits of our ancestors. Ancient Anatolian Cuisine and culture. Egyptian Cuisine culture. Chinese and Japanese cuisine. Persian Empire Culture and Cuisine. Roman Empire era culture and cuisine. Nutritional habits of South America. Central European Culture and cuisine. French cuisine ancestors of modern cuisine. South East Asia Cultures and Cuisine. Anatolian Cuisine with the rule of Ottoman Empire. Food Production and Service accompanied with beverages. Tea and Coffee Culture throughout the different cultures.

THM 326.name: Tourism Policies and Sustainability
THM 326.description: This course aims first to provide an understanding of sustainable development with its three pillars, and to examine how the concept was implemented in tourism industry. Tourism industry's positive and negative impacts on the environment, economies and communities, and its' stakeholders - will be discussed. Articles and real examples from the industry will be examined. Student term papers and presentations will focus on the questions of how mass tourism can be made sustainable what are the measures implemented by the global companies which lead the tourism industry.

THM 327.name: Event Management
THM 327.description: Historic development and importance of meetings and conventions, together with the terminology and classification. Prominent event destinations in the world and their attributes. Costing details and operation process of small to medium size events.

THM 328.name: Menu Planning and Design
THM 328.description: A Look Back at the Foodservice Industry, Planning a Food Menu, Considerations and Limits in Menu Planning and Design, Menu Pricing Strategies, Menu Psychology, Menu Engineering, Analyzing the Menu with respect to Nutrition, Hygiene in Menu Planning, The Beverage Menu, Sustainable Waste Management, Ethical Leadership in Restaurant Management.

THM 348.name: Service Operations Management
THM 348.description: The dimensions of successful service firms and enlightened management as well as creative entrepreneurial opportunities. The role of service in an economy, the nature of services, service strategy, new service development, service quality, process improvement, the service encounter, managing capacity and demand, and growth and globalization of services.

THM 390.name: Art of Pastry
THM 390.description: This course will prepare students for careers or post-secondary programs related to the baking and pastry culinary business and industry. The student will apply the knowledge and skills of how basic ingredients function, baking/pastry vocabulary, and mixing techniques to produce baking/pastry products based on industry standards. Students will develop skills in basic bread and pastry techniques to produce breads, muffins, biscuits, pies, cakes, pastries, and specialized desserts. Attention to detail and artistic flair are key skills that begin to develop during this class.

THM 391.name: Business Forecasting
THM 391.description: The course aims at presenting the basic statistical techniques used for business forecasts and long-term loans. The focus is on deriving meaning from a particular data set and the use of statistical estimation methods. Moving averages, simple and multiple regression, time series analysis and box-jenkins methodology are the topics of the course.

THM 392.name: Nutrition and General Health
THM 392.description: Fascination of the science of nutrition and the fun and excitement of nutrition. Understanding how the scientific facts apply to people's health in daily life.

THM 396.name: Case Studies for Tourism
THM 396.description: The purpose of the course is to cover the innovative techniques of defining different aspects of tourism and hospitality world's problem areas and exploring through the use of selected domestic and international case studies the solution of those.

THM 398.name: Food and Beverage Culture
THM 398.description: Knowledge for effective management of food and beverage services, conducted in two sessions. First, theoretical knowledge before the service starts, then experience by working in a fine dining rooms bar area. This course will prepare students for careers or post-secondary programs related to the food and beverage culture and services. The students will apply the knowledge and skills of how basic ingredients function, technologies; which will be useful for their professional career. Students will develop skills in mixology and to complete the service with their ritual.

THM 403.name: Organizational Behavior
THM 403.description: The analytical approach to studying organizational behavior. Introduction to organizational behavior discipline, diversity in organizations, emotions and moods, perception and individual decision making, motivation concepts, foundations of group behavior, communication, leadership, power and politics, conflict and negotiation, foundation of organization structure, organizational culture, and human resource policies and practices.

THM 409.name: Tourism Law
THM 409.description: Laws and regulations affecting our lives and specifically those that govern the operations in tourism industry. General legal system, concepts and applications, commercial law, consumer protection regulations as well as tourism regulations, travel agency regulations and legal background governing the operation of tourist guides.

THM 415.name: Finance
THM 415.description: Introduction to Financial Management, Understanding Financial Statements, Taxes and Cash Flows, The Time Value of Money - The Basics, The Time Value of Money Annuities and Other Topics, An Introduction to Risk and Return - History of Financial Market Returns, Risk and Return, Debt Valuation and Interest Rates, Investment Decision Criteria, Analyzing Project Cash Flows, The Cost of Capital.

THM 416.name: Revenue Management and Data Analytics
THM 416.description: History of Revenue Management, Fundamentals of Revenue Management: Customer Knowledge and Consumer Behavior, Market Segmentation, Internal Assessment and Competitive Analysis, Economic Principles and Demand Forecasting, Reservation and Channels of Distribution, Pricing Strategies: Dynamic Value-Based Pricing, Channel and Inventory Management, The Revenue Management Team, Strategic Management and Following the RevMAP, Tools, Tactics and Resources, Legal and Ethical Issues, Other Concepts of Revenue Management: Over Booking, Reputation Management. "Hotel Simulation" is used in this course.

THM 418.name: Senior Project
THM 418.description: A project on a given subject matter, enrich theoretical and practical refinement, and new trends in tourism industry.

THM 419.name: Strategic Management in Hospitality
THM 419.description: Introduction to strategic management approaches concerning the tourism industry worldwide. Strategic Management; corporate, business and functional level strategies. The corporate level strategies are analyzed comparatively, critical discussions about whether and how strategic models/theories can be applied into the hospitality and tourism industry. Tourism Industry Life Cycle, Human systems, and Appraisal of Lodging facilities. The Operating Budget, Feasibility study; Market profile analysis and Financial analysis. Vanguard management philosophy with the five characteristics.

THM 420.name: Seminars on Tourism Industry
THM 420.description: Weekly seminars by guest speakers from various tourism related industries.

THM 423.name: Tourism Economics
THM 423.description: In addition to theoretical aspects of tourism economy, Turkey's domestic, inbound and outbound tourism as well contribution of tourism industry to Turkey's national economy. Economic and accounting costs, firm's costs in the short and long run, economies of scale, firms' types of growth, market structures and tourism, price discrimination and tourism, externality and tourism, government intervention in the market, public goods and tourism, Turkey's tourism industry profile, inbound tourism expenditures, foreign inbound accommodation category, foreign inbound purpose of visit, outbound tourism expenditures, outbound purpose of visit, domestic tourism expenditure category, Tourism Satellite Accounts (TSA), analysis of Canadian Tourism Satellite Accounts, Turkey's Gross Domestic Products, Turkey's balance of payment, and Turkey's employment statistics.

THM 453.name: Total Quality Management
THM 453.description: The ways to set standards in hotels, restaurants, airlines and other hospitality companies to provide harmonious work and monitoring, evaluating and redesigning the quality requirements in tourism industry.

THM 460.name: Entrepreneurship and International Project Management
THM 460.description: Introduction to Entrepreneurship - course intro, team forming, overview of final project, Opportunity Identification - trends and tourism gaps in Turkey, Innovation in Hospitality, Business Model Design - value proposition, revenue models, Sustainability and Social Entrepreneurship, Digital Transformation, Creativity and Idea Development, Strategic Thinking, Intro to International Project Management, Cross-Cultural Management, Risk and Legal Environment, Funding and Partnerships, Project Planning + Monitoring and Evaluation.

THM 475.name: Strategic Marketing for the Hospitality Industry
THM 475.description: The strategies of management of the marketing function, the preparation of internal and external analyses, objectives strategies, action plans, and controls to develop and maintain a strategic fit between the organization's goals and capabilities/resources and its changing marketing opportunities. Guidance to the development and preparation of strategic planning of any hospitality operation.

THM 476.name: Research Techniques
THM 476.description: Main fundamentals of science, fundamentals of research, kinds of research and steps in the research process. Determination of methodology, selection of data collection techniques, analysis techniques and reporting phase.

THM 477.name: Planning for Profit
THM 477.description: Revenue management in hospitality industry; profit fallacy, differential pricing and pricing strategies, revenue optimization, relationship between quality and price, managing distribution channels, various analyses, legal and ethical aspects of revenue management.

THM 487.name: Concept and Design for Food and Beverage Outlets
THM 487.description: Basic knowledge for developing concepts for fine dining restaurants, cafes, fast food units and cafeterias. Choosing a good location, designing the interior and exterior of the restaurant, equipping the kitchen and the dining room and managing the pre-opening and opening phases of the restaurants.

THM 493.name: Nutritional Anthropology
THM 493.description: Culture and food relations in human population, inform eating habits and kitchen culture through history. Assigned readings, case studies and presentations as centerpieces on the complex dynamics of culinary arts and culture of different societies in the history.

THM 494.name: Digital Marketing
THM 494.description: The development of the Internet, World Wide Web and other digital technologies have transformed marketing and communicating with the current and prospective customers and the public in general. Therefore, this course will provide a solid foundation in the key concepts in digital marketing including strategy formulation for digital marketing, relationship marketing using digital platforms, campaign planning for digital media, marketing communications using digital media channels, evaluating and improvement of digital channel performance. Through case studies, students will learn best practice frameworks for developing a digital marketing strategy and success factors for key digital marketing techniques like conversion rate optimization and communications using social media including Instagram and Facebook.
